# TabList

The row of tab triggers inside `Tabs`, built on react-aria-components `TabList`. Renders `role="tablist"` and manages roving-tabindex focus for its `Tab` children. Give it an `aria-label` when there is no visible heading labelling the tab set.

Import: `import { TabList } from '@ds/react';` — the only public entry point.

Built on react-aria-components `TabList`; keyboard behavior, ARIA, and focus management ship inside. All `TabList` base props (e.g. event handlers, `isDisabled`, `autoFocus`) are also legal here, with the props listed below overriding or narrowing them.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes. Narrowed from the react-aria-components render-prop form to a plain string; inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |

Theming hooks: `--ds-tabs-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

## Accessibility

- Keyboard behavior, ARIA semantics, and focus management come from react-aria-components `TabList` — never re-implement or bypass them.
- Interaction states are exposed as data attributes (`[data-hovered]`, `[data-focus-visible]`, `[data-disabled]`, …); the focus-visible ring uses `var(--ds-color-border-focus)` and `var(--ds-shadow-focus-ring)`.
- Color pairs used by this system are contrast-audited (WCAG 2.2 AA (normal text)); see registries/contrast-report.json. Only audited foreground/background token pairs are legal.

## Examples

```tsx
<TabList aria-label="Account settings">
  <Tab id="profile">Profile</Tab>
  <Tab id="security">Security</Tab>
</TabList>
```
